citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- a numeric vector subset from the SAME 64-channel root the Welch/Hjorth/spectrogram/coherence cases use. The spatial map uses all 64 channels.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioEEG::svdEntropy(order=3, delay=1): time-delay embed the signal into an order-dimensional matrix, take the normalized singular values, and return their Shannon entropy. The reference re-computes it with antropy.svd_entropy (matched order + delay), via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the POz channel numeric vector, subset from agent/eval/data/hjorth-eeg/eeg64_s002r02.rds. SVD entropy (Roberts et al. 1999) is a linear-algebraic complexity measure: it embeds the signal in an order-dimensional delay space and reads the Shannon entropy of the embedding matrix's normalized singular-value spectrum -- an index of the signal's dimensionality (low = structured/low-dimensional, high = complex/high-dimensional). svdEntropy is a NEW op authored to fill this gap (the complexity suite had permutation entropy, Lempel-Ziv, Hjorth, sample/approximate entropy, DFA, RQA -- but not the singular-value view). It reproduces antropy.svd_entropy BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~2e-16) because R's svd() and numpy's np.linalg.svd both call LAPACK. The finding: SVD entropy is lower over the posterior (parieto-occipital) region (all 9 posterior channels below the frontal mean; posterior mean 1.239 vs frontal 1.287) -- the eyes-closed alpha rhythm is a comparatively low-dimensional oscillation, consistent with the Welch (high posterior alpha power), spectrogram (sustained alpha), Hjorth (low posterior mobility), and coherence (posterior alpha synchrony) cases on the same data.
